findings.finding: For a mobility-limited occupant (stairs avoided), every upstairs room (Landing, Master Bedroom, Kids' Bedroom, Upstairs Bathroom) has no secondary egress at all — the routing engine shows all four rooms' only route funnels through the single Master Bedroom window (w_master). If that window is blocked, smoke-filled, or unusable, occupants in the Kids' Bedroom or Bathroom who cannot use stairs have no way out.
findings.recommendation: Provide an accessible ground-floor sleeping option or ramp-based emergency exit for mobility-limited occupants, per fire-safety guidance to sleep near an accessible exit; consider installing a residential fire sprinkler system, which significantly increases available escape time for those who cannot use stairs or windows.

findings.finding: The Kids' Bedroom window (w_kids) fails code egress requirements: width is 0.40m (required minimum 0.508m/20in) and clear opening area is 0.40m², below the required 0.53m² (5.7 sq ft). This is the room's only alternate way out besides the door/landing/stairs route.
findings.recommendation: Replace the Kids' Bedroom window with a code-compliant egress window (minimum 20 in x 24 in clear opening, net clear area ≥ 5.7 sq ft, operable from inside without tools) so the room has a genuine second way out if the door/hallway route is blocked by fire or smoke.

findings.finding: The Upstairs Bathroom window (w_bath2) fails egress on three counts: height 0.60m (< 0.61m minimum), clear opening area 0.36m² (< 0.53m² required), and sill height 1.20m above floor (> 1.118m/44in maximum). It cannot serve as an emergency exit.
findings.recommendation: If feasible, upsize the bathroom window and lower the sill to meet IRC R310 egress minimums, or ensure occupants know this window is not a viable escape route and rely on the door/landing/stairs path instead.
